newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rain eases drought fear for spring cereals.
newsitem.headline: French rain eases drought fear for spring cereals.

text.p: A weekend burst of rain lifted some of the concerns over France's grain crop but will do little to address long-term water problems after months of dry weather, government experts and farmers said on Monday.
The rain was expected to help mostly spring crops as it came too late to bring big advantages to the winter crop.

"The rain made a dent in the drought situation and gave relief to the crops," a weather specialist at the environment ministry said. But the amount of rainfall was not enough to replenish water tables below the soil's surface.
National weather serice Meteo France measured the weekend's rainfall at 10-20 mm. Showers were also reported in the dominant grain producing region around Paris on Monday morning.
Forecasters expect cooler temperatures and some rainfall to last until at least mid-week.
A farm ministry official said the rain would do some good to the winter grain crop sown last autumn, but yields would still decline from record levels reached last year.
The rain however helped the growth of spring crops and in the southwest allowed farmers to get on with maize sowings.
The APCA farm lobby said spring crops may escape unscathed but there were worries over the fate of winter grains.
"The rain helped winter grain but will not make up for ground lost earlier," an official there said.
"If precipitation returns to normal levels we can hope yields will be in line with an average year," he said.
The spring grain crop is dominated by maize and about 40 percent of French barley is grown from spring varieties. But nearly all the country's wheat grows through the winter.

Weather experts say underground water resources are 25 percent below normal across three quarters of the French countryside. In about half the country, the deficit measured against the seasonal average has reached 50 percent.
Farmers are predicting irreversible damage to some crops and have been promised aid to help deal with losses.
Drought fears have pushed up domestic grain prices and forced authorities to limit irrigation in 23 provinces, including the Beauce grain producing area south of Paris.
But several experts remain wary of gloomy predictions after last year's crops managed to survive a similar drought scare.
National grain yields for the 1996 harvest jumped to a record 7.1 tonnes per hectare from 6.5 tonnes in 1995.
Total French grain production hit a record 62.46 million tonnes, 9.4 percent above the five-year average for 1990-1994.
